learning_outcomes.text: Convey basic knowledge for the systematic assessment of technical malfunctions, e.g., due to material wear or fracture, and develop robust solutions to increase the lifespan of technical products.

Students will gain a fundamental understanding of conducting a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and methodically clarifying the cause of malfunctions. To gain insights for the further development of sustainable components, Reverse Engineering techniques will be used, and the fundamentals of fracture mechanics explained.
Acquire the ability to argue linguistically and logically correctly and to communicate scientific facts understandably (assessment/evaluation).
Critical analysis of experimental results, including report writing.
Teamwork through working in small groups (communication, problem solving).

syllabus_topics: Definition of terms based on theoretical knowledge, standards, regulations
Instruments of a preliminary analysis, procedure and execution of a damage analysis
Presentation and discussion of damage cases from practical experience (collaboration with companies from the region)
Selection of suitable physico-chemical, electrochemical and mechanical investigation methods
Types of fractures, causes and topographies of fracture surfaces
Specific corrosion damage to components without and with mechanical stress
Correlation of results with possible damage mechanisms
Presentation of results / measures for damage prevention, if applicable, for further development of the component / process
Report writing and customer discussion (with invited industry partners)
Self-organization, critical questioning and report writing, interdisciplinary thinking, presentation of exercise tasks
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the presentation and report (grade). Successful participation in the practical training is a prerequisite for taking the exam.
